content.title: Victor Wembanyama, Zach Edey and tallest players in the NBA right now
content.text: A relative newcomer has taken the NBA to new heights. Victor Wembanyama arrived in San Antonio two years ago as one of the most coveted draft prospects of all time. At 7-foot-4, the French phenom brought unprecedented skill for someone his size. It didn’t take long for Wembanyama to start racking up NBA hardware. He was named 2023-24 NBA Rookie of the Year and earned a spot on the NBA All-Defensive first team while averaging a league-leading 3.6 blocks per game. A year after Wembanyama went first overall, another international behemoth was drafted in the top 10. The Memphis Grizzlies selected Zach Edey with the ninth overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Like Wembanyama at the time, the Canadian center out of Purdue stood at a towering 7-foot-4. Where do Wembanyama and Edey stand among the tallest players in the NBA? Let’s look around the league for the tallest current and all-time players. Who is the tallest player in the NBA right now? NBA Wembanyama has actually grown and is currently the tallest player in the NBA at 7-foot-5. 0:515 things to know about Zach Edey Here are five things you should know about Zach Edey. Who is the tallest player in NBA history? Gheorghe Muresan and Manute Bol are the tallest people to ever play in the NBA at 7-foot-7. Tacko Fall, Yao Ming, Slavko Vranes and Shawn Bradley are just a smidge shorter at 7-foot-6. Chuck Nevitt, Pavel Podkolzin, Sim Bhullar and Wembanyama are next in line at 7-foot-5. At 7-foot-4, Edey is tied with Ralph Sampson, Mark Eaton, Rik Smits, Priest Lauderdale and Boban Marjanovic as the 11th-tallest players in NBA history. Tallest player on each NBA team Here are the tallest players on each team according to their listed heights on NBA.com. Atlanta Hawks: Kristaps Porzingis – 7-foot-2 Boston Celtics: Neemias Queta – 7-foot-0 Brooklyn Nets: Nic Claxton and Danny Wolf – 6-foot-11 Charlotte Hornets: Ryan Kalkbrenner – 7-foot-1 Chicago Bulls: Zach Collins – 6-foot-11 Cleveland Cavaliers: Evan Mobley – 6-foot-11 Dallas Mavericks: Dereck Lively II – 7-foot-1 Denver Nuggets: Moses Brown – 7-foot-2 Detroit Pistons: Charles Bediako – 7-foot-0 Golden State Warriors: Quinten Post – 7-foot-0 Houston Rockets: Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun and Steven Adams – 6-foot-11 Indiana Pacers: Jay Huff – 7-foot-1 Los Angeles Clippers: Brook Lopez – 7-foot-1 Los Angeles Lakers: Deandre Ayton, Jaxson Hayes and Christian Koloko – 7-foot-0 Memphis Grizzlies: Zach Edey – 7-foot-4 Miami Heat: Kel’el Ware and Vladislav Goldin – 7-foot-0 Milwaukee Bucks: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Myles Turner – 6-foot-11 Minnesota Timberwolves: Rocco Zikarsky – 7-foot-3 New Orleans Pelicans: Hunter Dickinson – 7-foot-1 New York Knicks: Karl-Anthony Towns, Mitchell Robinson, Alex Len and Ariel Hukporti – 7-foot-0 Oklahoma City Thunder: Chet Holmgren – 7-foot-1 Orlando Magic: Moe Wagner – 6-foot-11 Philadelphia 76ers: Joel Embiid – 7-foot-0 Phoenix Suns: Mark Williams and Khaman Maluach – 7-foot-1 Portland Trail Blazers: Donovan Clingan – 7-foot-2 Sacramento Kings: Maxime Raynaud – 7-foot-1 San Antonio Spurs: Victor Wembanyama – 7-foot-5 Toronto Raptors: Jakob Poeltl – 7-foot-0 Utah Jazz: Walker Kessler – 7-foot-2 Washington Wizards: Alexandre Sarr and Tristan Vukcevic – 7-foot-0 Editor’s note: An earlier version of this article was published in October 2023.
